title: Simplified PESI (sPESI)
sources: Jiménez D et al. Arch Intern Med 2010; ESC 2019 Acute PE guideline
purpose: Predicts 30-day mortality after acute PE and identifies low-risk patients potentially eligible for early discharge / outpatient treatment. Each factor is 1 point; any point ≥ 1 = not low-risk.

items.label: Chronic cardiopulmonary disease (chronic heart failure OR chronic lung disease)
Arterial oxygen saturation < 90% (with or without supplemental O2)

interpretation.label: Low risk — 30-day mortality ~ 1.0%. Consider early discharge / outpatient anticoagulation if no RV dysfunction, no positive troponin, adequate home support, and follow-up secured (see Hestia criteria)

Not low risk — 30-day mortality ~ 10.9%. Admit. If haemodynamically stable, assess RV function (echo / CT) and troponin to separate intermediate-low from intermediate-high (the latter needs monitoring for rescue reperfusion)

notes: sPESI does not itself decide thrombolysis — it separates low-risk from everyone else. A haemodynamically unstable PE is high-risk by definition regardless of score. Pair with the Hestia criteria (which include bleeding risk, renal/hepatic failure, pregnancy, social factors) for the actual home-treatment decision.
